A cruder cross-check: ~2–2.6M/yr pre-1963 × ~100 years would already give ~200M+, so the order of magnitude is plausible. viruses.notes: No published all-time or 20th-century total for influenza found — the total must be assembled from components. Sum of 20th-century pandemics alone: ~17–100M (1918) + 1.1M (1957) + 1M (1968) ≈ 19–106 million (central ~52M). Seasonal flu adds ~0.29–0.65M/yr today (Iuliano); for earlier decades rates were higher but there is no global series — do not extrapolate on-screen without caveat. 1918 estimates disagree by >5x: Spreeuwenberg 2018 17.4M vs Johnson & Mueller 2002 50M (possibly up to 100M); CDC uses 'at least 50 million'; Patterson & Pyle 1991 gave 24.7–39.3M. 1957 and 1968: CDC 1.1M / 1M, other sources (Britannica, WHO) up to 1–4M each (>2x spread). 2009: CDC/Dawood 151,700–575,400 modelled vs WHO 18,449 lab-confirmed (30x gap — always use the modelled figure). GBD 2017 (145k) vs Iuliano (291–646k) differ >2x because GBD counts only influenza LRTI. The 1889–90 'Russian flu' (~1M) may have been a coronavirus (OC43) rather than influenza — do not include in influenza total without caveat. Double-count risk: none with other viruses, but excess-mortality methods can overlap with RSV/COVID in recent years.

discovered.detail: Walter Reed's US Army commission (Cuba, 1900–1901) proved mosquito transmission (Carlos Finlay's 1881 hypothesis) and showed the agent passed bacteria-proof filters — the first human disease shown to be caused by a filterable agent (virus). Virus isolated 1927 (Asibi strain, Stokes et al., Rockefeller Foundation, Ghana).

earliest_evidence.detail: Phylogenetics: current strains arose in Africa within the last ~1,500 years and reached the Americas via the slave trade ~300–400 years ago (Bryant, Holmes & Barrett, PLoS Pathog 2007). First well-documented American epidemic: Barbados/Yucatán, 1647–1648.

vaccine.detail: Max Theiler's live-attenuated 17D vaccine, first used 1937 (Brazil); Theiler won the 1951 Nobel Prize — the only Nobel ever awarded for a virus vaccine. One dose gives lifelong protection.

viruses.status_2026: Endemic in tropical Africa and South America (WHO fact sheet usually states 34 African + 13 Latin American countries — not re-verified, page blocked). South American resurgence: 2025 had the most confirmed cases since 2020 (346 cases, 143 deaths, PAHO); 34 cases and 15 deaths in Bolivia, Colombia, Peru, Venezuela by mid-Feb 2026; PAHO risk 'high'.
fun_fact: Yellow fever helped force Napoleon to sell Louisiana to the US in 1803.
The only Nobel Prize ever given for a virus vaccine went to the 1937 yellow fever shot.

viruses.notes: No credible all-time historical total exists — the user's hoped-for 'historic totals' could not be sourced. Documented epidemic tolls (tens of thousands each: Philadelphia 1793 ~5k, Haiti 1802–03 ~15–23k French soldiers, Mississippi Valley 1878 13–20k; plus many Caribbean/Brazilian/US Gulf/West African epidemics and the French Panama Canal effort) are far smaller than the modern modelled African endemic burden (~30–80k/yr). Modern annual burden: Garske 2014 (78k, CI 19k–180k, Africa 2013) vs Gaythorpe 2021 (51k, CI 31k–82k, Africa+S. America 2018) — older WHO wording cited 30,000–60,000/yr; serological assumptions can shift estimates nearly 20-fold (medRxiv companion work). WHO-reported confirmed cases are only hundreds/yr, several hundred-fold below modelled burden. Haiti figures disagree widely (15k in 2 months vs 23k total dead vs >50k all French losses) — primary source Girard 2005 not read. The WHO fact sheet could not be fetched (domain blocked). Louisiana fun fact: BnF heritage page states 'The failure of the Saint-Domingue expedition contributed to the Louisiana Purchase' and that a YF epidemic 'ravaged the expeditionary army' (~40,000 sailors and soldiers sent) — so on-screen wording should be 'helped' not 'caused'.
